resources.string: Describe the room: its size, the rows and columns of seats, and what the walls and floor are made of. You can also load a sample room to explore.
Find out how clearly people can hear at each seat. You clap at the front while the phone listens at a few seats, then it checks the background noise.
After measuring, you\'ll see which seats can follow the speaker, and whether echo, noise or distance is the problem.
Try cheap changes before spending money: curtains, switching off fans, moving the speaker or using a microphone. ClearRoom predicts how much each one helps.
Leave the phone in the room to see how background noise changes through the day. Only sound levels are kept, never audio.
Sample room loaded. Save it to keep your own copy.
Couldn\'t save the room. Check the phone has free storage, then try again.
That room\'s file couldn\'t be read.
The front of the room, with the speaker, is at the top.
Fill in the size and seats to see the floor plan.
Floor plan, %1$s by %2$s metres: %3$s of %4$s, speaker at the front.
Its measurements are deleted too. This can\'t be undone.
ClearRoom needs the microphone to measure sound levels. It never records or stores speech.
Without the microphone, ClearRoom can\'t measure the room. It only measures sound levels, never speech.
Microphone access is turned off for ClearRoom. Turn it on in Settings, under Permissions.
Set up or open a room on the Room tab first. Then pick the seat where the phone is.
The sample room is for exploring. Save it as your own room on the Room tab, then measure here.
Ready. Pick a seat, then choose a measurement below.
Listening to the background noise for %1$.0f seconds. Please keep quiet…
Recording the voice for %1$.0f seconds. Keep reading…
Measured, but the room couldn\'t be saved. Check the phone has free storage, then try again.
Too loud: the sound overloaded the microphone. Move the phone a little further away and try again.
No sound came through. Another app may be using the microphone, or it\'s muted.
Tap the seat where the phone is. The front of the room, with the speaker, is at the top.
Leave fans and AC as they usually are and say how they\'re set. Everyone keeps quiet while the phone listens.
Hold the phone 1 m from the speaker\'s mouth, at mouth height. The speaker reads this aloud in their normal teaching voice:

Good morning, everyone. Today we will look at how sound travels in this room. Please listen carefully, and raise your hand if any word is hard to hear. When we speak to a class, our voice has to reach the back row as clearly as the front. Let us find out how well it does.
dB relative to the phone\'s maximum. Only differences between readings matter.
Couldn\'t open the microphone. Close other apps that use it, then try again.
Microphone access was turned off. Allow it again to measure.
The recording stopped unexpectedly. Please try again.
